answer.content: DNS (Domain Name System) works by mapping domain names to IP addresses. The browser asks the local resolver for the IP address of a domain. If it doesn't know the answer, it queries a root server. The root server then directs the query to the appropriate top-level domain (TLD) server, which in turn directs it to the authoritative server for the domain. The authoritative server returns the IP address, which is then cached for future use. This process is facilitated by a hierarchical tree structure where each level of the tree (root, TLDs, second-level domains) provides the next level's information. [p. 2]
